A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same alt-test research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six LLMs across ten datasets, prompting comparisons, sensitivity studies, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised, bootstrap-averaged results for the advanced prompting comparison.

M1.justification: The core leave-one-out alignment, hypothesis testing, and BY correction procedure remains unchanged. Appendix A adds optional adaptations for rank inputs, combining disjoint annotator sets, and pooling FDR correction across domains; C.4 proposes minority-sensitive weighting adaptations.

E1.justification: The same ten datasets, annotation aspects, and language and vision-language tasks are evaluated. The new rank-based, subjective-task, and multi-domain scenarios are methodological guidance, without corresponding new evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains all six LLMs. Table 3 retains the same four closed-source models, prompting variants, and Gemini/GPT/all-model ensembles. Table 4 retains the same four embedding models.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes from reporting individual three-annotator, 100-instance subsets to averaging over resampled subsets of that size. This changes the reported sampling and aggregation design within the existing experiment. The full-dataset and sensitivity-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The instance-count and epsilon sensitivity studies, embedding comparison, annotation-aspect breakdowns, and SummEval distribution case study are retained. Several are relocated, but no new ablation, robustness question, or empirical test of the appendix adaptations is introduced.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly reports means over 100 bootstraps; v1 did not report resampling for that table. Figure 2 already used 100 bootstrap combinations and empirical 90% confidence intervals, which remain unchanged. This does not establish additional LLM generation runs.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises the advanced-judge findings, including which few-shot models qualify on SummEval. Winning rates for Gemini-Flash, Gemini-Pro, GPT-4o, and GPT-4o-mini change from 0.67/0.33/0.67/0.67 to bootstrap means of 0.41/0.59/0.28/0.77, reducing qualifying rows from three to two. These are revised estimates under different aggregation, not same-setting performance changes. Tables 2 and 4–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its proof are identical after relocation from Appendix B to D. The alignment, advantage-probability, IPW, annotator-quality, and BY mathematics are retained. The new practical adaptations add no formal theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The principal alt-test, average-advantage-probability, and optimal-judge contributions remain. v3 narrows superiority claims to the open-source models examined and summarizes success on nine datasets when prompting variants are included, versus v1's eight-dataset synopsis. The ninth dataset already had few-shot successes in v1.

C2.justification: The FAQ adds substantive qualifications about two-annotator reliability, combining annotators from different distributions, and scaling evaluation across many domains. Appendix C.4 explains minority-opinion considerations. A new footnote requires comparisons across model sizes before generalizing conclusions about model openness.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents a maximum pool of 300 annotated instances per dataset for bootstrapping and specifies the model name Llama-3.1-7B-Instruct. It drops v1's disclosure that advanced LGBTeen experiments focused on Q4, Q6, Q7, and Q10; whether that selection changed is unresolved. Prompts and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Trott (2024), removes Avalle et al. (2024) and the illustrative BERTScore citation, and condenses the discussion of prediction-powered inference. The central positioning against conventional alignment measures and statistical estimation work remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: a new FAQ opens the appendix, the cost-benefit and annotator-profile discussions move there, and the SummEval case study becomes Appendix B.3. Instance-count analysis moves into Results. The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and conclusion are also edited.

P2.justification: All four figures and six tables are retained. Figure 3 moves from the main text to the appendix. Table 3 adds bootstrap information to its heading and caption and changes the continuous-task column labels from Acc to Pears. Other changes mainly involve float placement and appendix layout.

improvement.justification: Bootstrap averaging strengthens the advanced-prompting comparison by reducing dependence on a particular small subset. The FAQ and narrower model-openness claims also clarify application and scope. These gains are limited: most scientific evidence is unchanged, the new adaptations are untested, and the LGBTeen question-selection disclosure is lost.
